thread:
lina: FYI — rolling out new service-identity guardrails tomorrow 09:00 UTC. This enforces permission boundaries and moves org-managed service accounts to short-lived credentials by default. Long-lived keys will be rejected for new SAs; existing keys need migration or an approved exemption. :warning:

lina: Summary: 1) Permission boundaries added to new identities. 2) Org policy blocks user-managed long-lived keys on creation. 3) 48h soft audit window, then hard enforcement.

aj: Does this touch our Dedicated/private customer infra?
lina: No, only Redwood org-managed identities and our infra project. We'll publish recommendations for private deployments.

chen: What do infra owners need to do now?
lina: Please: a) enumerate SAs with user-managed keys, b) rotate to OIDC/STS or workload identity, c) update automation that downloads JSON keys, d) request temporary exemptions with a justification and expiry.

lina: Quick GCP helper: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=... --format='table(name,validAfterTime,validBeforeTime)'`

lina: AWS: use the credential report and look for access keys older than 90 days.

Tom: Will Terraform modules be updated to attach permission boundaries automatically?
lina: Yes — new infra modules (v2.1.0) will set a default permission boundary. Opt-out requires an eng-security ticket. Module release ETA: 16:00 UTC today.

sarah: CI runners still relying on JSON keys — Jenkins jobs, etc. Migration plan?
lina: Migrate runners to workload identity federation or the credential helper. Jenkins migration doc: https://internal.redwood/infra/ci-migrate. If you need help, tag infra-oncall.

infra-oncall-bot: Reminder: automated audit will create tickets for noncompliant identities at enforcement time.

aj: Do we have ownership mapping for SAs? Need to know who to nag.
lina: Ownership CSV uploaded to the eng-security ticket. If your team appears unowned, assign an owner by EOD tomorrow.

chen: What if something critical breaks during enforcement?
lina: For first 48 hours enforcement is soft (logs + tickets). After that new key uploads will be blocked. We have rollback playbooks and an emergency suspend for critical incidents. If you see outages, open a ticket titled "iam-guardrails-incident" and @infra-oncall will respond.

ops-bot: deploy iam-guardrails canary finished: success 16:05 UTC :white_check_mark:

chen: Can we get a short runbook for rotating a key safely (commands + smoke checks)?
lina: Creating runbook now, will post to the ticket by 17:00 UTC.

infra-oncall-bot: Initial audit found 62 service accounts with user-managed keys flagged for review. Ticket: https://internal.redwood/engsec/tickets/RED-4221

lina: Thanks team. Enforcement starts: 2024-11-12T09:00:00Z. If you need an exemption open a ticket and include scope, justification, and ETA for remediation. Closing thread.
